SMTO-SKL-0077 — Microsoft 365 asked SMTO to slow down

GUID: 47257a59-7b23-5085-a0d5-aea1192900ed
Slug: microsoft365-graph-throttled
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • Microsoft is limiting how many requests SMTO can make right now, so it refused this one. Nothing was changed by this request; you just need to wait before asking again.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait at least a few minutes before asking SMTO to do anything else with Microsoft 365. If the error details give a wait time, wait at least that long. Microsoft keeps refusing requests until its waiting period is over.
  2. Ask for less at once, for example fewer emails, a shorter date range or one folder instead of everything. Smaller requests use up Microsoft's limit more slowly.
  3. Avoid running several Microsoft 365 tasks at the same time on this account. All of them count toward the same limit for your account.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the request after the wait without another slow-down message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO's Microsoft 365 setup. Don't repeat the request over and over; that keeps the limit in place longer.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Microsoft Graph returned 429 Too Many Requests; SMTO either already used its bounded read retries, the Retry-After delay exceeded 30 seconds, or the request was a write (which is not retried); retry_after_seconds carries the provider delay.

What this means

  • Graph returns HTTP 429 and bounded eligible read retries cannot proceed or have been exhausted. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Graph returns HTTP 429 and bounded eligible read retries cannot proceed or have been exhausted.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect retry_after_seconds and the affected operation.

How to fix it

  • Wait at least retry_after_seconds from the tool result before the next Graph request for this account, then repeat once. Reduce the page limit, narrow the search or date window, and avoid parallel Microsoft 365 tasks on the same account if throttling continues.
  • Wait at least retry_after_seconds before a new request. Reduce page size or query scope if throttling continues.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Further requests respect the provider's delay and original mutation state.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
